correct_diagnosis: Migrated plastic biliary stent impacted in Meckel diverticulum causing diverticulitis and adjacent ileal perforation

published_final_diagnosis.label: Migrated plastic biliary stent impacted in Meckel diverticulum causing diverticulitis and adjacent ileal perforation

source_treatment.description: Segmental small-bowel resection and primary anastomosis

source_disposition.outcome: ICU intubation; COPD-related respiratory failure; extubated after day 13; discharged postoperative day 40.

key_guideline_decisions.note: See docs/guideline_sources.yaml; applicability and alternative care require clinician review.

distractors: Mechanical bowel obstruction may seem adhesive until prior stent and CT foreign body are linked.
critical_safety_points: Peritoneal signs and obstruction demand urgent surgical assessment.
Prior biliary stent history materially changes interpretation of linear CT foreign body.
Consider anticoagulation and COPD risk during perioperative planning; source does not specify drug regimen.

source_locators: PDF pp. 1–2, preoperative CT description in case presentation

source_uncertainties: Unspecified dose, timing or normal findings were not inferred.
Published management is descriptive and requires separate normative review.
The CT case-presentation description identified a foreign body; the migrated biliary stent identity was established intraoperatively. After surgery the patient was transferred intubated to ICU.

critical_diagnoses_to_not_miss: Small-bowel obstruction with perforation or peritonitis requiring emergency surgery

expected_actions.deadline: Before final disposition when clinically indicated
Urgent abdominal exploration; laparoscopy with conversion to open surgery was the published sequence, but clinically justified open exploration is an acceptable alternative.
Surgery is the immediate handoff; ICU is source-supported after operation.
